_comment: Washi dictionary for the origins map. `desc`/`regionLabel`/`name` are the Japanese source terminology; `descEn`/`regionLabelEn`/`nameEn` are the English shown in English mode. Each region maps to one or more prefecture JIS codes (data-code in src/assets/japan-prefectures.svg); markerCode is the prefecture that carries the region's dot/label.

categories.name: 国指定・登録のある産地和紙
基本の和紙（原料による分類）
産地・製法に特有の和紙
装飾・加工された和紙

kozoshi.name: 楮紙
kozoshi.regionLabel: 那須・土佐・石州 ほか
kozoshi.desc: 日本で最も多く使われる和紙。太く強靭な繊維をもち、打紙加工や、米粉・胡粉などの填料を加えることで表情が大きく変わる。強度を要する和紙の中心的な存在。
kozoshi.descEn: The most widely used washi in Japan. Its thick, tough fibres change character markedly with beating (uchigami) or with fillers such as rice flour or gofun (shell white). The central paper wherever strength is needed.

ganpishi.name: 雁皮紙
ganpishi.regionLabel: 野生のジンチョウゲ科（栽培困難）
ganpishi.desc: 和紙のなかで最もなめらかで光沢があり、書写料紙として最上とされる。半透明で緻密なため虫害が少なく、記録保存にも適す。振ると甲高い音が鳴るのも特徴。
ganpishi.descEn: The smoothest and glossiest of all washi, prized as the finest paper for writing. Semi-translucent and dense, it suffers little insect damage and suits long-term records. Shaken, it gives a high, clear sound.

mitsumatashi.name: 三椏紙
mitsumatashi.regionLabel: 日本各地（近世以降に栽培普及）
mitsumatashi.desc: 雁皮ほどではないが光沢がある。繊維の強度は楮や雁皮にやや劣るが柔らかく、箔下紙などに使われた。
mitsumatashi.regionLabelEn: Across Japan (cultivated widely since the early modern period)
mitsumatashi.descEn: Glossy, though less so than gampi. The fibre is slightly weaker than kōzo or gampi but soft, and it served as the backing paper for gold and silver leaf.

mashi.name: 麻紙
mashi.regionLabel: 中国由来（古代に日本へ）
mashi.desc: 大麻や苧麻の繊維を用いた、中国から伝わった最も古い紙。繊維が非常に長く強靭だが抄紙に手間がかかり、平安時代以降は衰退。古代には広く使われた。
mashi.descEn: The oldest paper, brought from China, made from hemp or ramie fibre. The fibres are very long and tough, but sheet-forming was laborious and it declined after the Heian period. Widely used in antiquity.

kongoshi.name: 混合紙
kongoshi.desc: 楮と雁皮、三椏と楮など、複数の植物繊維を混合して漉いた紙。それぞれの繊維の特徴を併せ持つ。
kongoshi.descEn: Paper formed from a blend of plant fibres, such as kōzo with gampi or mitsumata with kōzo, combining the qualities of each.

misugami.name: 美栖紙
misugami.desc: 楮に胡粉や白土を混入した打紙。漉いた紙を板床に重ねて脱水し乾燥板で自然乾燥させる「簀伏せ」により、非常にやわらかく仕上がる。掛軸の増裏・中裏の裏打ち紙に用いる。「表具用手漉和紙（美栖紙）製作」として国の選定保存技術に選定されている。
misugami.descEn: A beaten kōzo paper with gofun (shell white) or white clay added. Freshly formed sheets are stacked on a board to drain and dried naturally on boards (subuse), which leaves the paper exceptionally soft. Used for the second and third linings (mashi-ura, naka-ura) of hanging scrolls. Its making is a nationally Selected Conservation Technique.

udagami.name: 宇陀紙
udagami.desc: 楮に白土を添加した紙。防虫効果があり、表装後に狂い（反りや波打ち）が生じにくい。掛軸の最後の裏打ちである総裏紙として重用される。「表具用手漉和紙（宇陀紙）製作」として国の選定保存技術に選定されている。
udagami.descEn: A kōzo paper with white clay added. It resists insects and, once mounted, rarely warps or ripples. Prized as the final lining (sō-ura) of hanging scrolls. Its making is a nationally Selected Conservation Technique.

suiharashi.name: 杉原紙
suiharashi.desc: 楮を原料とした紙。播磨・杉原谷が発祥とされ、中世には武家文書などとして広く使われた。
suiharashi.descEn: A kōzo paper said to originate in the Sugihara valley of Harima. In the medieval period it was widely used for the documents of the warrior class.

danshi.name: 檀紙 / 布目紙
danshi.reading: だんし / ぬのめがみ
danshi.regionLabel: 陸奥（東北）・讃岐 ほか
danshi.desc: 高級紙として珍重された。布目紙は麻布や絹布の間に湿紙を挟み圧搾して布目模様をつけたもの。近世初頭までの檀紙はこの布目紙で、現在の檀紙は乾燥の工夫で皺を寄せたもの。
danshi.descEn: Treasured as a luxury paper. Nunome-gami was made by pressing a wet sheet between hemp or silk cloth to leave a weave pattern. Danshi up to the early modern period was this cloth-textured paper; today’s danshi gets its crinkled surface from the way it is dried.

hoshogami.name: 奉書紙
hoshogami.desc: 米粉を填料として加えた楮紙。老中奉書などの公文書や高級な浮世絵に用いた。米粉ゆえ虫害に遭いやすく、現在は滑石（タルク）で代用されることが多い。
hoshogami.descEn: A kōzo paper with rice flour as filler, used for official documents such as rōjū hōsho and for fine ukiyo-e prints. The rice flour makes it prone to insect damage, so talc is often substituted today.

doroiri.name: 泥（土）入り間似合紙
doroiri.reading: どろいりまにあいがみ
doroiri.desc: 雁皮繊維に土（粘土）を添加して漉いた紙。表面が平滑で、水を通しても伸縮が抑えられる。色合わせ（間似合）などの装飾紙として作られ、襖の装飾にも用いる。
doroiri.descEn: A gampi paper formed with clay added to the fibre. The surface is smooth and it stretches little even when wetted. Made as a decorative paper for colour-matching (maniai), and used to decorate sliding doors.

kumogami.name: 雲紙・飛雲紙・羅文紙
kumogami.desc: 染め紙の技法の応用。雲紙は紙の上下2箇所に藍や紫の繊維を流し込み、飛雲紙は雲の形に散らし、羅文紙は着色繊維で網目状の文様を作った緻密な紙。
kumogami.descEn: Applications of dyed-paper technique. Kumogami has indigo or purple fibre poured in along the top and bottom edges; tobikumo scatters it in cloud shapes; ramonshi is a dense paper with a net-like pattern of coloured fibre.

suminagashi.name: 墨流し
suminagashi.desc: 水面に墨汁を落とし、松脂などで拡散させてできる流動的な文様を、紙に写し取った装飾紙。
suminagashi.descEn: A decorative paper that captures the flowing pattern made by dropping ink on water and spreading it with pine resin.

tsugigami.name: 継ぎ紙
tsugigami.desc: 種類・色彩・装飾の異なる紙を、破り継ぎや重ね継ぎで一枚に繋ぎ合わせたもの。西本願寺『三十六人家集』に見られる華麗な意匠が特徴。
tsugigami.descEn: Papers of different kinds, colours and decoration joined into one sheet by torn or overlapping joins. Known for the sumptuous designs of the Sanjūrokunin Kashū at Nishi Hongan-ji.

karakami.name: 唐紙
karakami.regionLabel: 京都（京唐紙）・江戸（江戸唐紙）
karakami.desc: もとは唐（中国）渡来の紙で、のち日本で模造された。胡粉を引いた紙の上に、雲母（きら）で版木文様を刷った装飾紙。
karakami.descEn: Originally paper brought from Tang China, later imitated in Japan. A decorative paper on which woodblock patterns are printed in mica (kira) over a gofun ground.

chiyogami.name: 千代紙
chiyogami.desc: さまざまな文様を木版で色刷りした紙。江戸時代に錦絵の影響を受けて発展した。
chiyogami.descEn: Paper colour-printed from woodblocks in a variety of patterns. It developed in the Edo period under the influence of nishiki-e prints.

senshi.name: 宣紙 / 竹紙
senshi.desc: 中国から輸入された、竹や青檀・稲藁などを原料とする紙。日本では主に書や水墨画に用いられ、江戸時代に国産の画仙紙が作られるきっかけともなった。
senshi.descEn: Paper imported from China, made from bamboo, blue sandalwood or rice straw. In Japan it was used mainly for calligraphy and ink painting, and prompted the making of domestic gasenshi in the Edo period.

etchu-washi.name: 越中和紙
etchu-washi.regionLabel: 富山県（五箇山・八尾ほか）
etchu-washi.desc: 五箇山・八尾などで漉かれる富山の和紙の総称。障子紙から型染めの民藝紙まで幅が広く、雪深い土地の楮を活かした強い紙で知られる。
etchu-washi.descEn: The collective name for the washi of Toyama, made at Gokayama, Yatsuo and elsewhere. It ranges from shōji paper to stencil-dyed folk-craft paper and is known as a strong paper that makes the most of kōzo grown in deep-snow country.

ogunigami.name: 小国紙
ogunigami.desc: 豪雪地帯の「雪さらし」で仕上げる楮紙。雪上に紙を広げて日光で自然漂白する製法が特徴で、柔らかな白と強さを併せ持つ。
ogunigami.descEn: A kōzo paper finished by “snow bleaching” in heavy-snow country: the sheets are spread on snow and bleached naturally by sunlight, giving a soft white together with strength.

echizen-washi.name: 越前和紙
echizen-washi.desc: 1500年の歴史を誇る日本最大級の産地。紙の神「川上御前」を祀り、奉書・鳥の子・襖紙・美術用紙まで、あらゆる高級紙を漉き分ける。
echizen-washi.descEn: One of Japan’s largest papermaking districts, with 1,500 years of history. It venerates the paper goddess Kawakami Gozen and makes every kind of fine paper, from hōsho and torinoko to sliding-door paper and paper for artists.

echizen-hosho.name: 越前奉書
echizen-hosho.desc: 楮の最高級厚紙。人間国宝・岩野市兵衛家が漉き継ぎ、浮世絵の復刻や版画用紙として世界の版画家に求められる。重要無形文化財。
echizen-hosho.descEn: The finest heavy kōzo paper. Made by the Iwano Ichibei family, holders of the Living National Treasure title, and sought by printmakers worldwide for reprinting ukiyo-e and for prints. Important Intangible Cultural Property.

echizen-torinoko.name: 越前鳥の子紙
echizen-torinoko.desc: 雁皮を主原料とする滑らかで丈夫な紙。卵殻色の紙肌から「鳥の子」と呼ばれ、料紙・襖紙の最高級品。重要無形文化財。
echizen-torinoko.descEn: A smooth, strong paper made mainly from gampi. Its eggshell colour gave it the name torinoko (“chick”); the finest grade of writing paper and sliding-door paper. Important Intangible Cultural Property.

uchiyamagami.name: 内山紙
uchiyamagami.desc: 楮100%を雪さらしで仕上げる信州の障子紙。通気性と保温性に優れ、日焼けしにくい強靭な紙として知られる。
uchiyamagami.descEn: A Shinshū shōji paper of 100% kōzo, finished by snow bleaching. Known as a tough paper that breathes, insulates and resists yellowing in sunlight.

inshu-washi.name: 因州和紙
inshu-washi.regionLabel: 鳥取県鳥取市佐治・青谷
inshu-washi.desc: 書道・水墨画用の画仙紙で全国有数のシェアを誇る産地。墨の濃淡が美しく出る滲みの調整技術に優れる。
inshu-washi.regionLabelEn: Saji and Aoya, Tottori, Tottori Prefecture
inshu-washi.descEn: A district with one of the largest shares of gasenshi for calligraphy and ink painting in the country. Its skill lies in tuning the bleed so that the tones of ink come out beautifully.

sekishu-washi.name: 石州和紙
sekishu-washi.desc: 石見地方で漉かれる楮紙。強靭さで知られ、かつて大阪商人が帳簿に使い「火事の際は井戸に投げ込んで守った」と伝わる。
sekishu-washi.descEn: A kōzo paper made in the Iwami region. Known for its toughness: Osaka merchants are said to have used it for their ledgers and, in a fire, to have thrown the ledgers down a well to save them.

sekishu-hanshi.name: 石州半紙
sekishu-hanshi.desc: 石州和紙のうち伝統製法を守る楮半紙。重要無形文化財であり、2014年「和紙：日本の手漉和紙技術」としてユネスコ無形文化遺産に登録された3紙の一つ。
sekishu-hanshi.descEn: The kōzo hanshi made within Sekishū washi by the traditional method. An Important Intangible Cultural Property and, since 2014, one of the three papers inscribed by UNESCO as “Washi, craftsmanship of traditional Japanese hand-made paper”.

hodomurashi.name: 程村紙
hodomurashi.desc: 烏山和紙を代表する厚手の楮紙。那須楮の強い繊維を活かした重厚な紙で、賞状用紙などに使われる。
hodomurashi.descEn: The thick kōzo paper that represents Karasuyama washi. A weighty paper that draws on the strong fibre of Nasu kōzo, used for certificates and similar.

nishinouchishi.name: 西の内紙
nishinouchishi.desc: 那須楮100%の強靭な紙。水に濡れても破れにくく、江戸時代には水戸藩の専売品として商人の大福帳に重用された。
nishinouchishi.descEn: A tough paper of 100% Nasu kōzo that resists tearing even when wet. In the Edo period it was a monopoly product of the Mito domain, prized by merchants for their daifukuchō account books.

mino-washi.name: 美濃和紙
mino-washi.desc: 1300年の歴史を持つ美濃の和紙。ムラのない薄さと美しさで「提灯・障子紙の最高峰」とされ、正倉院文書にもその名が残る。
mino-washi.descEn: The washi of Mino, with 1,300 years of history. Its even thinness and beauty make it “the finest paper for lanterns and shōji”, and its name appears in the Shōsōin documents.

honminogami.name: 本美濃紙
honminogami.desc: 美濃和紙のうち最も厳格な伝統製法による楮紙。重要無形文化財、そしてユネスコ無形文化遺産「和紙」構成3紙の一つ。障子紙の理想とされる。
honminogami.descEn: The kōzo paper made by the strictest traditional method within Mino washi. An Important Intangible Cultural Property and one of the three papers in the UNESCO “Washi” inscription. Regarded as the ideal shōji paper.

hosokawashi.name: 細川紙
hosokawashi.regionLabel: 埼玉県小川町・東秩父村
hosokawashi.desc: 武州楮による強靭な楮紙。江戸の商家の帳簿・記録用紙を支えた。重要無形文化財、ユネスコ無形文化遺産「和紙」構成3紙の一つ。
hosokawashi.descEn: A tough kōzo paper from Bushū kōzo that supported the ledgers and records of Edo merchant houses. An Important Intangible Cultural Property and one of the three papers in the UNESCO “Washi” inscription.

awa-washi.name: 阿波和紙
awa-washi.desc: 徳島の伝統産地。特産の藍で染めた藍染和紙が名高く、現代では美術用紙・インクジェット対応和紙など革新にも積極的。
awa-washi.descEn: The traditional district of Tokushima, famous for washi dyed with the local indigo. Today it also innovates actively, with paper for artists and inkjet-ready washi.

tosa-washi.name: 土佐和紙
tosa-washi.regionLabel: 高知県いの町・土佐市
tosa-washi.desc: 仁淀川の清流と土佐楮に育まれた産地の総称。薄紙から厚紙まで品種の多さは全国随一で、近代製紙の祖・吉井源太を生んだ。
tosa-washi.descEn: The collective name for the papers raised on the clear Niyodo River and Tosa kōzo. Its range, from the thinnest tissue to thick boards, is the widest in the country, and it produced Yoshii Genta, the father of modern Japanese papermaking.

tosa-tengujo.name: 土佐典具帖紙
tosa-tengujo.desc: 「カゲロウの羽」と呼ばれる世界最薄クラスの楮紙。厚さ0.02mmでも強く、ルーブル美術館や大英博物館など世界の修復現場で補修紙の国際標準として使われる。
tosa-tengujo.descEn: Among the thinnest kōzo papers in the world, called “mayfly wings”. Strong even at 0.02 mm, it is the international standard repair tissue in conservation studios from the Louvre to the British Museum.

seichoshi.name: 清帳紙
seichoshi.desc: 土佐の伝統的な楮の帳面紙。丈夫で墨のりがよく、帳簿・記録用として使われてきた。国選択の無形文化財。
seichoshi.descEn: The traditional kōzo ledger paper of Tosa. Durable and receptive to ink, it has served for account books and records. A nationally Selected Intangible Cultural Property.

ozu-washi.name: 大洲和紙
ozu-washi.desc: 肱川流域で漉かれる伊予の和紙。薄く均質な書道半紙で名高く、凧合戦で知られる五十崎の大凧にも使われる。
ozu-washi.descEn: The Iyo washi made along the Hiji River. Famous for thin, even calligraphy hanshi, and used for the great kites of Ikazaki, known for its kite battles.

senkashi.name: 泉貨紙
senkashi.desc: 漉いた紙を2枚重ねて1枚に仕上げる独特の製法による厚紙。非常に強靭で、江戸時代には帳簿や合羽に使われた。
senkashi.descEn: A thick paper made by an unusual method in which two freshly formed sheets are couched together as one. Exceptionally tough; in the Edo period it was used for ledgers and rain capes.

yoshinogami.name: 吉野紙
yoshinogami.desc: 楮の極薄紙。柔らかく毛羽立ちが少ないため漆漉しに最適とされ、「漆濾紙」とも呼ばれる。製作技術が国の選定保存技術。
yoshinogami.descEn: An ultra-thin kōzo paper. Soft and with little fuzz, it is the ideal filter for lacquer and is also called urushi-koshi paper. Its making is a nationally Selected Conservation Technique.

designations.name: ユネスコ無形文化遺産
